notes.2: Many candidates appreciated that organisms only belong to the same species if they can breed and produce fertile young. Some were not aware that the offspring must be fertile.
notes.4: Most candidates were not aware that chlorophyll contains magnesium.
notes.6: Many candidates were aware that the experiment demonstrated diffusion, some believed this to be absorption or osmosis.
notes.7: Candidates showed a good understanding of how to calculate a magnification.

notes.11: The majority of candidates chose the correct option, some believed that boiling amylase makes it work faster.
notes.12: Many candidates were aware that root hair cells did not possess chloroplasts.
notes.13: This question was well-answered, showing a good understanding of the role of fibre in the body.
notes.14: Most candidates were able to work out which length was represented by the small intestine.
notes.15: Whilst many candidates correctly recognised the cause of obesity, some believed that obesity is caused by an increase consumption of dietary fibre. �PAGE�7
notes.16: There appeared to be some uncertainty about the meaning of the terms used in human nutrition, in particular, the terms ‘absorption’ and ‘assimilation.’
notes.17: While many candidates correctly recognised the structure as representing the phloem, there was some uncertainty as to whether the organ was a root or a stem.
notes.18: The definition of transpiration was known by most candidates.
notes.19: Most candidates correctly identified the blood vessel as an artery, some opted for a capillary or a vein.
notes.20: There was some uncertainty about which blood vessel carries blood directly from the lungs.
notes.21: There appeared to be some uncertainty as to what a mechanical barrier to pathogens is.
notes.22: Many candidates were uncertain about the composition of oxygen in exhaled air.

notes.general_comments:
The exam paper provided a good balance of questions and challenge at this level. The meanings of terms
‘species’ and ‘assimilation’ were not widely understood. The presence of magnesium in chlorophyll was also
not well known. Some candidates were also unclear about the definitions of diffusion and osmosis.
Identifying an artery from a diagram proved to be challenging for some candidates. The use of dichotomous
keys and how to calculate a magnification were well understood, and the definition of transpiration was
known by most candidates.
